abstract.text: Giving every window its own container instead of sharing one global.

inlineContent.text: is not scene aware. It never was.
On an iPhone with a single window you will never notice. On iPad with Split View or Stage Manager, or on the Mac, one process hosts several scenes at once. Every one of them resolves through the same
, with the same registrations and the same scope caches.
That’s the problem in one sentence. Here’s what it looks like in practice.
Two windows, two accounts. Both windows ask

for a session, and both get the same cached instance. Sign in on the left and the right window is suddenly looking at someone else’s data. Register a mock in one window and you’ve registered it in all of them.

There are other issues as well, but basically we need to stop trying to replace the global and figure out a way to give each scene its own container and let the views find it.
Fortunately, Apple gave us a solution. With a catch, of course.

But there’s a problem here. The Environment isn’t available on View initialization, and that’s where we usually need to construct our view models or setup access to our repositories or other services.
